thread:
maria: kicked off affinity-threshold experiment in eu-west1 (patching scheduler -> affinityThreshold=0.6) at ~10:03 UTC. seeing a cascade of preempts/evictions, flagging here :eyes:
vikram: which clusters/azs? can you share the exact flag you flipped?
maria: eu-west1-{a,b,c}, only the non-prod overlay group. intended to pack more tightly to save nodes. changed from 0.8 -> 0.6 via configmap.
sam: any sample pods that got bounced repeatedly?
maria: lots of tiny-worker pods and model-loaders. behaviour summary: pod X evicted on node-a -> scheduled to node-b -> preempted lower-priority pods on node-b -> autoscaler saw reduced requested capacity and scaled down node-c -> more preempts. looped for ~5 minutes.
infra-bot: autoscaler: eu-west1-b scaled down -12 nodes at 10:05:23 UTC (reason: low utilization).
elaine: kubelet logs show bulk evictions with reason "Evicted" / "Preemption" around 10:04-10:09. sample: ```
# kubectl get pods --field-selector=status.phase=Failed -o wide | grep Evicted
tiny-worker-7f8d9   Evicted   node-a   10:04:12
model-loader-2c4b1   Evicted   node-b   10:04:38
```
vikram: did the scheduler score function change, or just the threshold?
maria: only threshold. scheduler scoring still uses affinity + spill penalty but lowering threshold made more candidate nodes "eligible" even with lower locality, so it prefers tighter packing at pod-level, which triggered preempts.
sam: paste the patch you applied (so we can roll back fast).
maria: patch we used: ```
kubectl -n kube-system patch configmap scheduler-config -p '{"data":{"affinityThreshold":"0.6"}}'
# then rollout restart deployment/scheduler
```
sam: rolling back now -> setting affinityThreshold=0.8 and restarting scheduler replicas.
infra-bot: action: ConfigMap patched -> affinityThreshold=0.8 at 10:08:41 UTC. Restarting scheduler pods (3 replicas).
elaine: telemetry: reschedule rate peaked at ~210 pods/min during the window, scheduler CPU spiked to 88% -> flaky leader election logs.
vikram: root cause hypothesis: lowering threshold increased scoring churn for tiny pods; combined with autoscaler's aggressive scale-down on non-prod overlay, nodes removed faster than the scheduler's stabilization window, causing cascading preemptions.
maria: mitigation checklist executed: rollback threshold, pause scale-down for 10m on eu-west1 overlay, add temporary scheduler queuing throttle.
sam: created PR to add a per-pod cooldown (min-stable-seconds) and node-reschedule-rate-limit: PR #1234. short-term we can set min-stable-seconds=30 for tiny pods.
vikram: longer-term suggestions: 1) prefer stability metric in scoring (penalize nodes with recent evictions), 2) add autoscaler tie-break to avoid scale-down during heavy reschedule windows, 3) add a soft cap on reschedules per node/min.
elaine: cost hit estimate: +12 nodes * 6 minutes ~ ~0.12 node-hours -> rough charge ~ $3.8k? (need invoice calc) — capture in postmortem.
maria: will open incident doc and capture timelines + dashboards. also adding a test run in staging that simulates tiny-pod churn before changing threshold.
sam: for immediate ops: keep scale-down paused for eu-west overlay for 15m, watch evictions metric and scheduler CPU.
infra-bot: autoscaler: scale-down pause applied to overlay-eu-west at 10:10:02 UTC.
vikram: thanks, good catch. let's not re-run wider until fixed heuristics are in.
maria: noted. will follow up with postmortem and next steps. thanks all :thumbsup:
